articles.title: We asked real people what they’re wearing this fall – burgundy, secretly comfy pants and fierce boots
articles.summary: I chased down people on weekdays, interrupting their brisk walks and lunch breaks to ask them to share details of their fall outfits. ‘Is nonstick cookware safe?’ Send us your food safety questions.
body: I t’s October and New Yorkers have finally retired the breezy pants and linen button-downs required to brave stuffy subway stations. Like much of the US, we’re now tasked with expertly layering for autumn’s up-and-down weather while still looking put together for the workday.

You might also be staring down your closet’s sea of denim and bulky coats, wondering what to wear. Instead of consulting the runways or analyzing the latest fashion trends, I wandered through Manhattan’s financial district, which boasts millions of square feet in office space, to ask people about their outfits.

I chased down people on weekdays, interrupting their brisk walks and, most likely, their lunch breaks. Below, New Yorkers (and two visitors) share the details of their fall outfits. We couldn’t find exact matches for many of the items, so we linked to similar options, usually from the brands that they recommended.

articles.title: Modern life is stuck in a sea of sameness. The pursuit of beauty is a necessary antidote | Brigid Delaney
articles.summary: Everything has become so frictionless and optimised, that concerted efforts must be made to turn back towards beauty and individuality – even if it has no explicit market value. By the time it’s 5pm on a Friday, the headache and dry eyes have well and truly settled in.
body: To lift your spirits, you decide to treat yourself to a weekend at a beachside Airbnb.

But the town is not how you remember it as a kid. The farmland has been turned into identical housing estates broken up by highway-hugging shopping centres with the same Guzman, Woolies, Chemist Warehouse, Dan Murphy’s and Priceline as all the other shopping centres.
They’re not the only things that are samey. The cars in the car park are mostly white or grey, and stepping out of them, people are in near-identical athleisure or shorts and T-shirts.

The Airbnb is how it was depicted in the pictures (minimalist, fancy handwash in the bathroom, Anko soft furnishings) but there is something dispiriting about it. Just like the cars, the interior is grey and white, and it smells of surface cleaner. It’s a house devoid of colour, personality and character.
points: Everything has become so frictionless and optimised, that concerted efforts must be made to turn back towards beauty and individuality – even if it has no explicit market value.

articles.title: Experts cast doubt on Anthropic report detailing how AI has altered work at the company
articles.summary: Anthropic claims AI will shift how work gets done and labor demand – but some experts are skeptical of the vision. Last year, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned that artificial intelligence could eliminate half of entry-level white-collar jobs and that in six months it would be writing 90% of code.
body: Now, in a report Anthropic published on Thursday, the company said it was hiring fewer junior technical workers and that human attention has become the new “bottleneck” as it increasingly relies on its Claude AI agents.

Anthropic says AI has changed the way work gets done, and as a result, restructured employment at the company. The report suggests its changes foreshadow the future of work more broadly: as more companies adopt AI agents, software engineers could face a tougher job market while entry-level tech workers struggle to build necessary skills and experience.

“As AI diffuses and improves, the organization of work could shift,” Anthropic’s report reads before offering a potential future. “One possibility is single-person startups, each with a human founder steering swarms of agents to rake in billions in revenue.”

In its report, Anthropic touts its “deep adoption of AI”, which it claims resulted in “producing more code per person, closing more sales per rep, and processing more contracts”. By outsourcing some coding and sales-related tasks to AI agents, Anthropic said it raised productivity within a few months.
points: Anthropic claims AI will shift how work gets done and labor demand – but some experts are skeptical of the vision.

articles.title: Crowded nest? How parents and their adult kids can live together in peace
articles.summary: With record numbers of adult children living at home with their parents, how can this arrangement work for everyone? Set ground rules from the off, respect each other’s privacy, and don’t revert to type, say the experts.
body: Whether they are fresh out of university and looking for a job, have recently been made redundant, are saving to buy a home or newly divorced, it’s becoming increasingly common for adult children to live at home with their parents. According to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), 35% of men and 22% of women aged between 20 and 34 were living with their parents in 2025.

I speak from experience: my younger sister lived at home with my mother for two years while she did her PhD, and I moved home for almost three years after becoming a single mother postpartum. In both of our situations, it would have been good to have some practical advice to make it work, with tensions sometimes running high and arguments inevitable.

If parents and their adult children are going to coexist successfully, honest communication is essential from the outset. How long do children expect to stay? Will they contribute financially? Will they do any housework? Are guests allowed? Difficulties will arise if you aren’t clear about these boundaries from the off.

articles.title: Even Drake Can’t Resist the Siren Song of a Boho Fall
articles.summary: Move over Kate and Dakota! Drake, out celebrating his 40th birthday, made a compelling case for fall’s most free-spirited trend in a fringed poncho.
body: There are certain names that will forever be synonymous with boho style, but Drake has made a compelling case for adding his own to the compendium.

Of course, there’s Kate Moss, her shaggy coats and denim short-shorts; Sienna Miller and her penchant for waistcoats and ruffled skirts; and more recently, Daisy Edgar-Jones and Dakota Johnson, who fly the flag for a softer, more contemporary take on the free-spirited fashion. Drizzy, as the latest addition to the boho brigade, has his own take.

The rapper, who turns 40 tomorrow, was spotted heading to an early birthday dinner at Mamo restaurant in New York City, dressed in a look that wouldn’t have been entirely out of place in Moss’s or Miller’s mid-aughts wardrobe. The centerpiece was a sweeping, chestnut-brown poncho, its generous silhouette and long, swishing fringe bringing that distinctly bohemian sensibility to an otherwise pared-back outfit. Beneath it, Drake wore a simple black crewneck knit, straight-cut black leather trousers, and black boots.
points: Drake, out celebrating his 40th birthday, made a compelling case for fall’s most free-spirited trend in a fringed poncho.

articles.title: 8 Black-Tie Outfit Ideas for Your Most Glamorous Events
articles.summary: Your complete guide to mastering the black-tie outfit this fall, from statement fringe and bright tones to elegant draping and minimalist silhouettes.
body: The season of galas, formal weddings, and festive celebrations is upon us—and as invitations begin to flutter into your mailbox, you’ll need to start planning something very special to wear. Black-tie events are a chance to take your personal style to the max and indulge in your fanciest looks, whether you lean toward over-the-top gowns in bold hues or prefer sleek, minimalist classics. Luckily, the market is full of dazzling pieces ready to meet every interpretation of the dress code with ease, from chic column dresses to fluid satin gowns and sequin styles.

The reality, however, is that formal dressing is notoriously tricky terrain, and finding something polished yet modern can feel like a puzzle. The secret to getting it right? Let one standout element do the talking. Sculptural clutches or statement earrings can effortlessly elevate a simple dress—and since fall and winter soirées come with a chill, an eye-catching coat or wrap can do just as much work as your gown.
points: Your complete guide to mastering the black-tie outfit this fall, from statement fringe and bright tones to elegant draping and minimalist silhouettes.

articles.title: Victoria Beckham’s Second Gap Collection Reimagines Fall’s Essential Layers
articles.summary: Beckham shares the inspiration behind her second collab with Gap—a 37-piece collection built around fall staples, including knits outerwear, and jeans.
body: Earlier this year, when designer Victoria Beckham released her inaugural collection for Gap, it sold out almost as fast as it landed. Shoppers vied to get their hands on the iconic brand’s heritage denim, button-downs, khakis, and hoodies, all reworked with the sharp tailoring and sleek silhouettes Beckham is known for.

On October 23, Gap and Victoria Beckham are returning with the second collection that carries that same signature polish into pieces for the colder months ahead, this time building upon it with cozy knits and statement outerwear. “I wanted to explore proportion, silhouette and color, balancing structure with an elevated sense of ease,” Beckham shares with Vogue. “I was inspired by the idea of taking Gap’s familiar wardrobe staples and reinterpreting them through my own design lens.”

articles.title: Reed All About It: Here’s How Alexander Skarsgård Wound Up in Couture Scuba Pants for ‘Wicker’
articles.summary: Costume designers András Dániel Tóth and Attila Godena-Juhász were given nine days’ notice to create a bottom half for Alexander Skarsgård’s Wicker Man.
body: Just over a week before Wicker began filming in Hungary, costume designers András Dániel Tóth and Attila Godena-Juhász, who work together as András + Attila, were thrown one big curveball. Alexander Skarsgård, who plays—as the title suggests—a man made entirely out of wicker, was only supposed to show skin from the waist up.

“The directors [Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson] came up with this idea nine days before we started to shoot that they would like to see Alex completely naked,” Tóth says. The duo and their team of costumers got to work fashioning Skarsgård a bottom half—wood and all. “We had nine days to catch up with Wētā Workshop [who created the prosthetic top half] and to finish the whole costume,” Tóth adds.
points: Costume designers András Dániel Tóth and Attila Godena-Juhász were given nine days’ notice to create a bottom half for Alexander Skarsgård’s Wicker Man.
